findings.message: The quoted formulation materially alters the Court's language. Anderson asks whether the evidence presents a sufficient disagreement "to require submission to a jury," not whether it presents disagreement "upon any essential element."

details.claim: The essential point for the court is "whether the evidence offered [in Rule 56 practice] presents a sufficient disagreement upon any essential element ..., or is it so one-sided that one party must prevail as a matter of law." Anderson v. Liberty (1986), 477 U.S. 242, 251-252.

tests.claim: Identify residential premises landlord and tenant or former tenant in possession.
tests.problem: The brief identifies Cazeau's Red Hill Drive residence and alleges that Stone lived there with Cazeau and remained an occupant until excluded. It characterizes Stone as an at-will occupant and later a tenant at sufferance, but the cited material as described primarily supports occupancy and social-guest status rather than clearly establishing a residential landlord-tenant relationship.
tests.reason: The quoted brief language establishes that Stone occupied Cazeau's residence at his will or sufferance, but it does not identify facts showing a rental agreement or otherwise clearly establish the residential landlord-tenant relationship required for the statutory theory. This creates a concrete support concern, though the supplied material does not conclusively establish that no qualifying tenancy existed.

tests.claim: Identify exclusion utility or service termination unlawful threat or seizure without required judicial process.
tests.problem: The brief alleges that Cazeau and Nixon changed the locks repeatedly, excluded Stone from the residence, and did so before or without Chapter 1923 process. It cites Stone's affidavit, attached notices, and appellees' answer admitting that Nixon changed the locks.
tests.reason: The brief specifically alleges lock changes, exclusion from the residence, and lack of Chapter 1923 process, and attributes those facts to Stone's sworn testimony and Nixon's written statements. The supplied evidence supports pleading the prohibited self-help act; the absence of independently supplied record excerpts does not establish a defect.

tests.claim: Plead actual harm causally resulting from the prohibited act.
tests.problem: The brief alleges that the lockouts prevented Stone from retrieving clothing, papers, craft materials, and other belongings, which appellees allegedly retained and never returned. The brief cites Stone's affidavit for the continued presence of her belongings, but no supplied record excerpt independently confirms the alleged loss, retention, value, or resulting damages.
tests.reason: The brief alleges a concrete resulting harm: exclusion prevented Stone from accessing belongings that appellees allegedly retained and never returned. That allegation identifies harm causally connected to the alleged lockout. Lack of an independent excerpt establishing value or ultimate damages does not establish a pleading defect.

rule_audit.name: Prohibited self-help recovery of possession or rent
rule_audit.label: Prohibited self-help recovery of possession or rent (R.C. 5321.15)
rule_audit.summary: A residential landlord may not recover possession through utility termination, exclusion, or other unlawful acts, and may not seize tenant property for rent without a court order.
rule_audit.excerpt: the residence several times, all to oust Alice. And on February 28, 2005, Edwin Cazeau issued Alice a statutory notice to quit the premises in three days but the door locks had already been changed. RC § 5321.15 provides that a person entitled to immediate possession of a residential dwelling can not exclude a tenant from the premises and can obtain possession only as provided in RC Chapter 1923. A person that violates RC § 5321.15 is liable for all damages caused as well as reasonable attorney

elements.requirement: Identify residential premises landlord and tenant or former tenant in possession.

elements.quote: Alice Stone's status in Cazeau's Red Hill residence was that of an occupant staying at the will or sufferance of Cazeau. While Cazeau could revoke or terminate Alice's at will occupation of his property, he was statutorily prohibited from distraining her property and access to the residence without process.

elements.quote: According to her sworn testimony, Alice Stone had been first excluded from the 815 Red Hill Drive residence on February 21, 2005. See Alice Stone Affidavit at P 8-10. By her own writing, Defendant Cathryn Nixon has admitted that she excluded Alice Stone. See exhibits one and two of Alice Stone Affidavit, saying to Alice "[D]o not enter the house [. ]" and that "[All] lock (sic) have been changed."

rule_audit.label: Prohibited self-help recovery of possession or rent (R.C. 5321.15)
rule_audit.summary: A residential landlord may not recover possession through utility termination, exclusion, or other unlawful acts, and may not seize tenant property for rent without a court order.
rule_audit.excerpt: the residence several times, all to oust Alice. And on February 28, 2005, Edwin Cazeau issued Alice a statutory notice to quit the premises in three days but the door locks had already been changed. RC § 5321.15 provides that a person entitled to immediate possession of a residential dwelling can not exclude a tenant from the premises and can obtain possession only as provided in RC Chapter 1923. A person that violates RC § 5321.15 is liable for all damages caused as well as reasonable attorney
